L0@P0: Meeting: LLC Board
L1@P0: Date: September 14, 2022
L2@P0: Attendees
L3@P0: LLC Board:
L4@P0: Lars Eggert
L5@P0: Jason Livingood
L6@P0: Peter Van Roste
L7@P0: Staff/Secretariat:
L8@P0: Jay Daley
L9@P0: Stephanie McCammon
L10@P0: Alexa Morris
L11@P0: Laura Nugent
L12@P0: Lee-Berkeley Shaw
L13@P0: Robert Sparks
L14@P0: Lisa Winkler
L15@P0: Greg Wood
L16@P0: Observers/Guests:
L17@P0: Sandy Ginoza
L18@P0: Scribe:
L19@P0: Michelle Cotton
L20@P0: Conflicts of Interest Declared:
L21@P0-1: None.Part I: Open to the Public
L22@P1: 1. Record e-vote results
L23@P1: One e-vote has been completed since the previous Board meeting.
L24@P1: a. The May 2022 financial statement was approved with the board e-voting as follows:
L25@P1: Maja Andjelkovic: YES
L26@P1: Lars Eggert: YES
L27@P1: Jason Livingood: YES
L28@P1: Sean Turner: YES
L29@P1: Peter Van Roste: YES
L30@P1: 2. Review & approve prior month's financial statement
L31@P1: No financial statement was ready for this meeting so review and approval will take place by
L32@P1: email.
L33@P1: 3. Update on the IETF's technical work
L34@P1: Lars reports that it is mostly business as usual as everyone starts to get ready for IETF 115.
L35@P1: The IESG held their first call for BOF requests. There are potentially 7 or 8 for London. The
L36@P1: IESG is also starting the 360 degree reviews. This will allow Area Directors to get feedback on
L37@P1: how they are doing and use the review for their own self improvement. There is some feedback
L38@P1: that the IESG is slow and drafts are getting stuck in the queue. Lars has reviewed the overall
L39@P1: queues for any spikes or trends. There does not seem to be anything out of the ordinary
L40@P1: happening and so he will continue to monitor it.
L41@P1-2: 4. Executive Director Report - PublicPublic Executive Director Report
L42@P2: For the IETF Administration LLC Board meeting on 14 September
L43@P2: 2022
L44@P2: This report is provided by the IETF Executive Director and is read through at the
L45@P2: meeting as it is not available to observers. This report is public and there is no
L46@P2: separate confidential report.
L47@P2: 1. Strategic Matters
L48@P2: Annual report
L49@P2: The 2021 Annual Report is now published. There is still an open question on this
L50@P2: report - waiting as we do now until the audited accounts can be included means
L51@P2: that this report is not ready for several months until the end of the year. The
L52@P2: alternative would be to publish it in January without any financial information and
L53@P2: then publish a financial addendum later in the year. Any views on this are welcome.
L54@P2: Annual planning and budget process
L55@P2: As the annual budget process is about to start, would the board like to review the
L56@P2: strategy or continue with our current budget assumptions?
L57@P2: 2. Policies
L58@P2: Misuse of IETF systems / Restricting participant access
L59@P2: As a reminder, we started a consultation on this on 7 August 2022 and that has now
L60@P2: closed. The IESG has discussed this and decided that they should be the decision
L61@P2: makers on any policy given that any sanctions may have an impact on the standards
L62@P2: process. They have asked the LLC to draw up a draft and hold the pen for future
L63@P2-3: versions. It is expected that a draft will be with the IESG by IETF 115.Antitrust
L64@P3: I have met with Counsel and can report that the training video is almost ready for
L65@P3: release. It would be worthwhile considering how this is distributed - should we play
L66@P3: it at plenary for example? The I-D is still under development and I expect to see a
L67@P3: draft soon after the board meeting.
L68@P3: OFAC Compliance
L69@P3: Counsel has recommended some changes to our OFAC Compliance Policy (tracked
L70@P3: changes shown). This requires board approval.
L71@P3: Recommendation: That the board approves the revised OFAC Compliance Policy.
L72@P3: This will be sent for e-vote after the meeting.
L73@P3: 3. Finance
L74@P3: Audit
L75@P3: The audit is now complete and the audited accounts have been published. It is likely
L76@P3: that ISOC will continue with the same auditors for another year.
L77@P3: New bank accounts
L78@P3: We have started the process of opening new bank accounts with the aim of
L79@P3: migrating away from our current bank due to their recurring poor service. We will be
L80@P3: liaising with the Treasurer on the mechanics of getting it up and running.
L81@P3: 4. RFPs and contracts
L82@P3: UI/UX Services
L83@P3: We are now in negotiation with a preferred bidder. This is likely to be completed and
L84@P3-4: announced by the time of the board meeting.Salesforce Integration Partner
L85@P4: This has closed and is at the evaluation stage.
L86@P4: 5. Meetings
L87@P4: IETF 114 Philadelphia
L88@P4: IETF 114 Philadelphia was by all accounts a successful meeting, though a few of us
L89@P4: spent it in a hotel room and missed the fun. As documented in a joint paper, our
L90@P4: COVID management policy was a success and the meeting did not become a
L91@P4: super-spreader event.
L92@P4: It will be a while before we have the full finances of the meeting to report.
L93@P4: IETF 115 London
L94@P4: Following an extensive consultation, the COVID management policy has been
L95@P4: decided and communicated.
L96@P4: Future meetings
L97@P4: We are close to finalising the bookings for IETF 121 (Europe, November 2024) and IETF
L98@P4: 122 (Asia, March 2025). Work on IETF 119 (March 2024) is well underway after being
L99@P4: delayed by COVID travel restrictions.
L100@P4: Carbon emissions measurement and mitigation
L101@P4: As a reminder, our aim is to develop and maintain an emissions calculator and to see
L102@P4: if we can get community support for some form of carbon offsetting.
L103@P4: We have largely completed the planning for a short series of workshops that will be
L104@P4: run by our appointed consultants. The first will cover measurement of emissions, the
L105@P4: relevant standards, what data we have to drive this and the various factors that are
L106@P4: taking into consideration, while the second will cover what carbon offset schemes
L107@P4-5: are, how they work, how they are evaluated and the economic models behind them.6. Tools/RPC/RSOC/RSE
L108@P5: Moving off tools.ietf.org
L109@P5: This move is finally complete and tools.ietf.org has been decommissioned and
L110@P5: redirections are in place.
L111@P5: RSCE recruitment
L112@P5: Alexis Rossi has been appointed as the RFC Series Consulting Editor. She has met
L113@P5: with multiple members of the community and begun to work closely with the RPC
L114@P5: and so overall her induction process is going well. I want to note my thanks to the
L115@P5: community members who participated in this process and who were a pleasure to
L116@P5: work with.
L117@P5: Wiki migration
L118@P5: We held a successful “contentathon” at IETF 114 where a number of staff, secretariat
L119@P5: and community volunteers moved a number of old wikis over to the new
L120@P5: wiki.ietf.org. This work is picking up pace with a number of WG chairs asking for a
L121@P5: migration and we hope to complete this work around IETF 115.
L122@P5: 7. IESG/IAB/IRTF/Trust
L123@P5: AD 360 Survey
L124@P5: We are again supporting the IESG with their AD 360 survey.
L125@P5: IAB Website
L126@P5: The IAB are looking at revamp of their website, which we will consider funding in
L127@P5-6: 2023 as our priorities for 2022 are set.8. Communications/Outreach/Engagement
L128@P6: Brand values project
L129@P6: This work is now complete and a set of Brand Voice Guidelines have been produced
L130@P6: for staff to use when communicating, particularly when developing collateral to
L131@P6: support our fundraising work.
L132@P6: 9. Miscellaneous
L133@P6: Nothing to report.
L134@P6: 5. Discuss Qs from IETF-114 about entry into Japan for IETF-116
L135@P6: Rules for entry into Japan may be changing. Currently there is nothing new to report and we
L136@P6: will be monitoring any announcements.
L137@P6: 6. Brief host’s view readout from IETF-114
L138@P6: Jason, in his role as a co-sponsor of the meeting (Comcast), related that the meeting went well.
L139@P6: But one of their key organizers contracted COVID the first day of the meeting and had to
L140@P6: quarantine.
L141@P6: He noted that there was one time when Comcast, which provided connectivity, assisted with a
L142@P6: network issue for Meetecho. This ended up being an off-net issue, but otherwise the network
L143@P6: seemed good.
L144@P6: There was also a heads up related to a potentially disruptive individual (they also alerted
L145@P6: appropriate hotel staff). By pre-arrangement, this was passed onto Comcast’s Global Security
L146@P6: Operations Center, which was tracking the security environment in Philadelphia related to the
L147@P6: IETF meeting and which maintains a liaison with the local police department (because the
L148@P6: company's headquarters was a few blocks walk away from the IETF venue). Thankfully no
L149@P6: issues arose and no contingency plans had to be used.
L150@P6: 7. AOB & Questions from Observers
L151@P6: The November Board meeting falls during IETF 115. An in-person meeting will be scheduled
L152@P6-7: during the meeting week in London.Part II: Board + Staff
L153@P7: 1. Ongoing Projects and Fundraising Update
L154@P7: The Salesforce RFP shortlisted vendors are currently being interviewed and we should be able
L155@P7: to have contracts by early October.
L156@P7: Lee-Berkeley is working on planning a hybrid multi stakeholder networking event in London with
L157@P7: Mallory Knodel and Andrew Campling, with Article 19 and CDT as hosts. She held multiple
L158@P7: meetings with organizations that expressed potential fundraising support, however with the
L159@P7: recent economic downturn budgets are tight. She will continue to engage with them.
L160@P7: 2. Future meetings
L161@P7: The Secretariat is currently looking at potential social events in London.
L162@P7: Brief updates on meeting locations/contracting for IETF 119-126.
L163@P7: Part III: Board + ED Only
L164@P7: Some details of future meeting contracts and potential sponsors were discussed.
L165@P7: The 2023 budget process was also discussed. The Board reiterated that as bottoms-up budgets
L166@P7: are built, that Jay should encourage the IETF Trust to put in a full budget request to the IETF
L167@P7: LLC so they do not need to perform independent fundraising.
L168@P7: Part IV: Board Only
L169@P7: The Board discussed some confusion concerning the financial reporting process and
L170@P7: statements and designated Peter to take up the issue for further discussion with Jay. The main
L171@P7: question was what the right mechanism was to bring more focus to accounting and reporting,
L172@P7: such as whether we should provide resources for part-time accounting staff.
